reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents flash-loan arbitrage as an easy way to double BNB and guides viewers through deploying and executing the associated smart contract. It ties the claimed return to supplying approximately 0.25 BNB per 1000 BNB borrowed and reports nearly doubling the original balance. Although it describes the material as educational and acknowledges possible failure and changing gas costs, those qualifications do not remove the concrete promotion of a high-return result tied to the instructed financial action.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation does not describe a guaranteed return. It says opportunities depend on market movement, warns that an attempt can fail, and notes that gas prices vary. Those qualifications matter when assessing the speaker's reported success: an account of one successful attempt is not, by itself, a promise that viewers will get the same result.

citations.quote: they depend on the movement that there is in the market and is the possibility that it finds in the exchange in question
Sometimes, arbitration can fail due to BNB's exhaustion in its intelligent contract, since the price of gas varies from time to time.
we have almost doubled what I had originally

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing reading treats the gas figure and execution steps as proof of a promised payout. But the speaker describes the amount as a minimum needed according to the contract code, while the description explicitly warns that execution can fail as gas prices change. The steps establish an attempted transaction; they do not establish a guaranteed result for every viewer.

citations.quote: for every 1000 BNB that we ask loan we need as a minimum according to the contract code about 0.25 BNB
Sometimes, arbitration can fail due to BNB's exhaustion in its intelligent contract, since the price of gas varies from time to time.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning that an attempt might fail does not neutralize the financial pitch. The description tells viewers to fund the deployed contract with BNB and execute it, while the speaker reports that the outcome nearly doubled the original balance. The risk language qualifies that pitch; it does not change what viewers are being urged to try.

opening.argument: Judge, the central sequence is an operational demonstration. The speaker introduces making a contract, then walks through creating a Solidity file, compiling it, and using Remix's deployment interface. The description also calls the video educational. A reported outcome appears at the end, but the material spends its attention showing a workflow; that supports reading it as a technical tutorial rather than treating the outcome as its sole purpose.

citations.quote: we will see how to make a flash loan type contract within the Binance Smart Chain network
We go here to this icon, create new file and we will place the name of Flashlogan.bsc.sol Once created, paste the code.
We change the version 5.0 and we proceed to compile. It was compiled perfectly.
The present video is educational

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing statement accurately identifies deployment and execution instructions, but instructions are also what make a tutorial usable. It does not show that explaining those steps is merely a pretext. The speaker begins by saying the video will show how to make a contract, and the walkthrough includes file creation and compilation before the reported result.

citations.quote: we will see how to make a flash loan type contract within the Binance Smart Chain network
We go here to this icon, create new file and we will place the name of Flashlogan.bsc.sol Once created, paste the code.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Tutorial form does not make the instructed transaction incidental. The description calls this a way to gain crypto, directs viewers to pay BNB into the deployed contract and execute its action, and says profits will be credited to their wallet after successful execution. The technical steps are the means offered for obtaining the advertised return.

citations.quote: it is a way to gain some crypts using the arbitration method using Smart Contracts (flashloan).

Once all these processes have been successfully executed, the transaction profits will be accredited in their wallet

opening.argument: Judge, the described payment has a specific operational explanation: the speaker says the BNB supplies gas so the contract can interact with protocols. The instructions concern deploying a contract through Remix and executing its action. The supplied account does not establish that viewers are sending funds to the creator, handing over credentials, or joining a recruitment scheme. A claimed profitable demonstration deserves scrutiny, but those absent elements should not be assumed from a contract-gas instruction.

citations.quote: What we are doing is giving the necessary gas so that they can act interact with the protocols
Pay the gas of your intelligent contract implemented with the BNB you have (0.25bnb per 1000BNB borrowed).
then proceed to execute the contract. Display the option that REMIX and we go to the action function.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument correctly notes that viewers are told to supply BNB, but its quoted instruction calls that payment gas for their implemented contract. Neither that wording nor the instruction to click Transact identifies a payment to the speaker. The reported gain may be unverified, yet the cited steps alone do not establish where the supplied BNB ultimately goes.

citations.quote: Pay the gas of your intelligent contract implemented with the BNB you have (0.25bnb per 1000BNB borrowed).
Click Transact to implement when it is finished.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A direct transfer to the speaker is not necessary for the concern here. Viewers are told to paste contract code from a supplied link, fund the deployed contract with BNB, and execute it. The speaker then presents a near-doubling as the result. Calling the payment gas does not verify the code's behavior or the claimed return.
